declarations.RDF11.Set: A set is represented by a membership proposition for each possible element. It has no positions, order or duplicate occurrences.
declarations.RDF11.Set.empty: The empty set contains no elements: every membership proposition is false.
declarations.RDF11.Set.singleton: The singleton containing a consists exactly of elements equal to a.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union: An element belongs to the union when it belongs to either input set.
declarations.RDF11.Set.subset: s is a subset of t when every member of s is also a member of t.
declarations.RDF11.Set.image: An element belongs to the image when some original member is mapped to it. Several originals may have the same image.
declarations.RDF11.Set.ofList: Interpret a list by membership alone. Repeated occurrences do not create additional set members.
declarations.RDF11.Set.ext: Two sets are equal if every element belongs to one exactly when it belongs to the other. The proof uses equality of propositions and functions.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union_idempotent: Taking the union of a set with itself gives exactly the same set.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union_comm: Swapping the two sets in a union does not change its members.
declarations.RDF11.Set.union_assoc: Regrouping three unions does not change their members.
declarations.RDF11.Set.subset_refl: Every set is a subset of itself.
declarations.RDF11.Set.subset_trans: If every member of s is in t, and every member of t is in u, then every member of s is in u.
declarations.RDF11.Set.ofList_repeat: The list [a, a] and the list [a] denote exactly the same set.
declarations.RDF11.Term: An RDF term has exactly one of three tagged forms: IRI, literal, or blank node. The tags keep the categories distinct even if their underlying representations coincide. The concrete IRI and literal domains remain abstract.
declarations.RDF11.Subject: An ordinary RDF subject is an IRI or a blank node. There is no literal constructor, so a literal subject cannot be constructed at this type.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.toTerm: View an admissible ordinary subject as a general RDF term, preserving its IRI or blank-node identity.
declarations.RDF11.Triple: An ordinary triple has three fields: an IRI-or-blank subject, an IRI predicate, and any RDF term as object. The field types enforce these position restrictions.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple: A generalized triple allows an IRI, literal or blank node in any of its three positions. This is wider syntax than an ordinary RDF triple.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.generalize: Embed an ordinary triple into generalized syntax without changing any of its three RDF terms.
declarations.RDF11.Graph: An ordinary RDF graph is a set of ordinary triples. Duplicate membership and triple order are not extra graph data; the definition does not assume a finite graph.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph: A generalized graph is a set of generalized triples. It retains set identity while allowing the wider triple syntax.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.generalize: Embed every ordinary triple of a graph into generalized syntax, taking the set of the resulting triples.
declarations.RDF11.Term.hasBlank: Test whether this term is the specified blank node; IRIs and literals do not contain blank nodes.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.hasBlank: A blank node occurs in a generalized triple if it occupies any one of its three positions.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.hasBlank: A blank node occurs in a graph if at least one member triple contains it.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.ground: A graph is ground when no blank node occurs in it.
declarations.RDF11.Term.hasLiteral: Test whether a term is the specified literal.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.hasLiteral: The specified literal occurs if it occupies at least one position of this generalized triple.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapBlank: Apply f to blank-node identities, leaving every IRI and literal unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapBlank: Apply the same blank-node mapping to all three positions of this triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank: Apply the same blank-node mapping throughout the graph and collect the resulting triples as a set.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapBlank_id: Leaving each blank-node identity unchanged leaves every term unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapBlank_comp: Renaming a term first by f and then by h equals renaming once by the composite function h after f.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapBlank_id: Identity blank renaming leaves the entire triple unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapBlank_comp: Two successive blank renamings of a triple equal one composed renaming.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank_id: Identity blank renaming leaves the graph equal as a set.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation: A simple interpretation packages IR (resources), IP (properties), IEXT (property extensions), IS (IRI denotation) and partial IL (literal denotation). IR is nonempty. IR and IP may overlap; this structure does not assume every property is a resource.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Resource: A resource is an element of the ambient universe together with evidence that it belongs to IR.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Property: A property is an ambient element together with evidence that it belongs to IP.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Assignment: A blank assignment is a partial function from blank identities to resources. The separate AssignmentOn condition constrains its exact domain for a graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.AssignmentOn: The assignment is defined exactly for the blank nodes occurring in G: every occurring blank gets a resource, and no unused blank does.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote: This is the extended interpretation [I+A]: IRIs use IS, literals use partial IL, and blanks use A. The result may be undefined.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.TripleTrue: A triple is true when its predicate denotes a property, its subject and object denote resources, and that resource pair belongs to the property extension IEXT.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.GraphTrue: With one fixed assignment A, every member triple of G must be true.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.Satisfies: I satisfies G when there exists one assignment for exactly G’s blank nodes that makes all G’s triples true. The same assignment witnesses the whole graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.restrict: Remove assignment entries for blank nodes that do not occur in G, retaining all entries used by G.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_agrees: Assignments agreeing on the blanks in a term give that term the same denotation.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_ag: Assignments agreeing on the blanks in a triple give it the same truth value.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graphTrue_res: Removing assignment entries unused by G does not change whether all its triples are true.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_bl: A true triple has a defined resource assignment for every blank node occurring in it.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_iff: To prove satisfaction it is enough to find an assignment making every triple true, even if it initially assigns unused blanks. The proof restricts that assignment to the exact graph domain.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_emp: Every interpretation satisfies the empty graph, since there are no member triples whose truth needs checking.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_sub: An interpretation satisfying G also satisfies any subgraph H: restrict the witnessing assignment to the blanks used by H.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.undefined_lit: A triple with an object literal whose IL value is undefined cannot be true.
A generalized triple with an undefined literal in any position cannot be true.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graph_with_un: If a graph has a member triple containing an undefined literal, this interpretation cannot satisfy the graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ground_satisf: For a graph with no blanks, satisfaction is equivalent to truth of every triple under the empty assignment.
declarations.RDF11.SimplyEntails: G simply entails E when every simple interpretation satisfying G also satisfies E. The quantification covers every carrier type in an arbitrary fixed Lean universe, not just a finite sample or a particular algorithm.
declarations.RDF11.LogicallyEquivalent: Two graphs are logically equivalent when each simply entails the other.
declarations.RDF11.simplyEntails_refl: Every graph entails itself: the same satisfaction proof is enough.
declarations.RDF11.simplyEntails_trans: Entailment composes: if G entails H and H entails E, G entails E.
declarations.RDF11.subgraph_entailment: Every graph entails each of its subgraphs, because truth of every member triple implies truth of the selected subset.
declarations.RDF11.premise_monotonicity: Adding triples to a premise cannot remove a simple entailment it already had.
declarations.RDF11.entails_empty: Every graph entails the empty graph, which is true in every interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.indiscriminate: This witness interpretation has one resource/property and makes every property pair true; all names denote that same element. It is used to prove existence of a model, not to restrict interpretations generally.
declarations.RDF11.all_graphs_simply_satisfiable: Every graph has a simple model, even if the graph is infinite. The proof uses the one-element indiscriminate interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.noPairs: This one-element interpretation has empty property extensions, so no triple is true. It provides a countermodel when needed.
declarations.RDF11.empty_entails_only_empty: If the empty graph entails E, then E has no triples. Otherwise the interpretation with empty property extensions would refute E while satisfying the empty premise.
declarations.RDF11.EntailsUnder: Entailment under extra conditions C quantifies only over simple interpretations satisfying C, retaining the same graph truth conditions.
declarations.RDF11.extension_preserves_simple_entailm: A simple entailment survives restricting interpretations by additional conditions C.
declarations.RDF11.stronger_conditions_preserve_entai: If every interpretation meeting D also meets C, then every entailment under C is valid under D.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_mapBla: Evaluating a renamed term under A is the same as evaluating the original under the assignment that first follows the renaming.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_ma: The same pullback of assignments preserves truth for a renamed triple.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graphTrue_map: The same pullback of assignments preserves truth of all triples in a renamed graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_map: If I satisfies the graph after a blank-to-blank mapping, then I satisfies the original graph. Pull back the witnessing assignment.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graphTrue_uni: Under one fixed assignment, a union is true exactly when both component graphs are true under that same assignment.
declarations.RDF11.merge: Merge first places the two graphs’ blank nodes in disjoint left/right domains, then takes the union of their renamed triples. This prevents accidental sharing.
declarations.RDF11.satisfies_merge: I satisfies the merge exactly when I satisfies each graph separately. The separate assignments combine because the renamed blank domains are disjoint.
declarations.RDF11.union_entails_merge: The union entails the merge: one shared assignment that satisfies the union supplies separate witnesses for both graphs.
declarations.RDF11.renamed_entails_original: Every blank-to-blank image of a graph entails the original. The mapping need not be injective, so this includes identification of blanks, not only bijective renaming.
declarations.RDF11.Substitution: A substitution optionally assigns an RDF term to each blank identity. An omitted entry means leave that blank unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Substitution.resolve: Look up a blank’s replacement; if no replacement was specified, return the original blank term.
declarations.RDF11.Term.substitute: Replace a blank once by its resolved image, leaving names fixed. This is simultaneous substitution: a replacement is not recursively substituted again in the same application.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.substitute: Use one substitution consistently in the subject, predicate and object positions.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.substitute: The substituted graph is the set of substituted member triples. If several triples become identical, they are one set member.
declarations.RDF11.IsInstance: H is an instance of G when some substitution produces exactly H from G. In IsInstance H G, H is the result and G is the original.
declarations.RDF11.InstanceWithVocabulary: An instance relative to V uses only names from V when replacing occurring blanks. Names already in G are preserved and need not belong to V.
declarations.RDF11.Substitution.then: Compose two substitutions by applying the second to each resolved image of the first. This represents two successive simultaneous substitutions.
declarations.RDF11.Term.substitute_id: A substitution with no specified replacements leaves a term unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Term.substitute_comp: Substituting a term twice equals one application of the composed substitution.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.substitute_id: Leaving every blank unchanged leaves the whole graph unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.substitute_comp: Substituting a graph twice gives the same set as applying the composed substitution once.
declarations.RDF11.instance_refl: Every graph is an instance of itself; use the substitution that leaves every blank unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.instance_trans: An instance of an instance is an instance of the original graph; compose the two substitutions.
declarations.RDF11.instance_triple_origin: Every triple in the substituted graph has at least one original member triple whose substitution produces it.
declarations.RDF11.ProperSubstitution: A substitution is proper for G when it replaces an occurring blank by an IRI or literal, or identifies two distinct occurring blanks. Collisions with an unchanged blank count; unused ambient identities do not.
declarations.RDF11.ProperInstance: H is a proper instance of G when a proper substitution produces it. This does not say H is a proper subgraph of G.
declarations.RDF11.LeanGraph: A graph is lean when every instance that is also a subgraph equals the graph itself. Thus no instance is a proper subgraph. This is RDF leanness, not the proof assistant’s name.
declarations.RDF11.ground_substitute: Substitution cannot change a ground graph, because the graph contains no blanks to replace.
declarations.RDF11.ground_is_lean: Every ground graph is lean. All its instances equal the graph, so none can be a proper subgraph.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank_comp: Two successive blank renamings of a graph equal one renaming by their composite function.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapBlank_of_fixes: A blank mapping fixing every blank that occurs in G leaves G unchanged; its behaviour on unused identities is irrelevant.
declarations.RDF11.mapBlank_is_instance: Every blank-to-blank mapping is a term substitution and therefore produces an instance.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism: An isomorphism supplies forward and inverse blank renamings, inverse on the blanks actually occurring in the graphs, with the forward image equal to H. IRIs and literals stay fixed. Unused ambient blank identities need not be bijective.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.inverse_image: Applying the inverse renaming to H gives exactly G. This follows from the forward image equality and the inverse law on G’s occurring blanks.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.mutual_instances: Isomorphic graphs are instances of one another, using the forward and inverse blank renamings.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.satisfies_iff: Every fixed simple interpretation satisfies G exactly when it satisfies an isomorphic H. The proof transports assignments in both directions.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.equivalent: Isomorphic graphs mutually entail each other. This is logical equivalence, not equality of their original blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.resourceDenot: Evaluate a term, keeping the result only if it belongs to IR. This is necessary because a blank assignment must be resource-valued and an arbitrary IRI may denote a property outside IR.
If a term is known to denote a resource r, resourceDenote returns precisely r.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.pullback: Assign each original blank the resource denoted by its replacement under A. Recompute every blank’s assignment, including identities also appearing in the image graph.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_pullba: If a substituted term denotes resource r, the original term denotes the same r under the pulled-back assignment.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ordinary_trip: Truth of an instance of an ordinary triple implies truth of that original triple under the pulled-back assignment. Its predicate is an unchanged IRI; subject and object truth provide resource witnesses.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_substitution_entails: Every term-substitution image of an ordinary RDF graph entails the original. One assignment is pulled back for the entire graph. The image may use generalized syntax; the source must be ordinary.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_instance_entails: For two ordinary RDF graphs, if H is an instance of G then H simply entails G. The ordinary endpoint types exclude literal subjects and non-IRI predicates.
declarations.RDF11.ordinary_instance_subgraph_equival: For ordinary graphs, a subgraph that is also an instance is logically equivalent to the original: subgraph entailment goes one way and instance entailment the other.
declarations.RDF11.instance_subgraph_entails: If a graph G contains an instance of ordinary E as a subgraph, then G entails E. This proves the sufficient direction of interpolation; the converse is not proved here.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration: A finite representation of set G carries a list, a no-duplicates proof, and a proof that list membership exactly matches G. An arbitrary plain list cannot satisfy this contract.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.unique: Remove repetitions from a finite list using decidable equality.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.unique_nodup: The list returned by unique has no duplicate elements.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.mem_unique: Removing repetitions preserves exactly which elements belong to the list.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.fromList: Convert any finite list into a certified enumeration of its represented set, removing repetitions and proving both membership and uniqueness.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.count_le_one: In a certified enumeration, every element occurs at most once.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.length_independent: Any two certified enumerations of the same set have equal lengths. Set size cannot depend on duplicated storage occurrences.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.repeated_input_same_se: Repeating an input element does not change the set represented by that input list.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.I: A two-resource interpretation used to distinguish separately witnessed graph truth from truth under a shared blank assignment.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.triple: This example triple uses the shared blank as subject, a Boolean-selected IRI as predicate, and the fixed IRI false as object.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.graph: The singleton graph containing the selected example triple.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.witness_forced: Truth of this example triple forces its blank assignment to the resource selected by v.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.each_satisfiable: Each example graph is satisfiable separately, by choosing its own required blank assignment.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.union_not_satisfied: The union is false in this interpretation because its shared blank would have to denote two different resources.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.merge_satisfied: The merge is true: its renamed blank domains permit independent resource witnesses.
declarations.RDF11.ScopeExample.merge_does_not_entail: This countermodel proves that a merge does not in general entail the union with shared blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.I: A simple interpretation with a property outside IR, permitted by the current literal reading of the source conditions; it exposes the generalized-predicate scope question.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.originalTriple: The generalized counterexample triple has a blank in predicate position.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.original: The singleton graph containing the generalized counterexample triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.substitutedTriple: Replace the predicate blank by IRI p, keeping the subject and object IRI s.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.substituted: The singleton graph containing that substituted triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.original_false: The original generalized graph is false in this interpretation: its predicate blank cannot be assigned the property outside IR.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.substituted_true: With distinct s and p, the substituted graph is true in the counterexample interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedScope.unrestricted_gene: The exhibited generalized instance does not entail its original under these truth conditions. This is evidence for a source-scope review question, not a declared W3C erratum.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IR: The resource domain, a set of elements of the ambient universe.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IR_nonempty: Evidence that the resource domain contains at least one element.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IP: The property domain. This field alone does not require IP to be a subset of IR.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IEXT: For each property, its extension is a set of ordered pairs of resources.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IS: An IRI denotes an element in the union of the resource and property domains.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.IL: A literal may be undefined; when defined it denotes a resource.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.subject: Select the subject field from this ordinary RDF triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.predicate: Select the predicate field from this ordinary RDF triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.object: Select the object field from this ordinary RDF triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.subject: Select the subject field from this generalized triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.predicate: Select the predicate field from this generalized triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.object: Select the object field from this generalized triple. Its permitted terms are enforced by the field type.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.toFun: The forward map on blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.invFun: The inverse map on blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.left_inv: For every blank occurring in G, going forward and then back restores its identity.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.right_inv: For every blank occurring in H, going back and then forward restores its identity.
declarations.RDF11.GraphIsomorphism.image_eq: Renaming every blank in G with the forward map gives exactly H as a set of triples.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.triples: The finite list carrying the enumeration.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.nodup: Evidence that no element occurs twice in the enumeration list.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.membership: Evidence that list membership is equivalent to membership in the represented set.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Atom: A source atom records a half-open Unicode scalar interval and the claim or unresolved record IDs assigned to it.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Contains: Position i belongs to an atom if start ≤ i < stop.
declarations.Spec2Lean.ValidPartition: The atoms must cover the specified interval consecutively, with positive lengths, nonempty reference lists and only known record IDs. This is structural accountability, not semantic completeness.
declarations.Spec2Lean.partitionDecidable: Compute whether a finite atom list meets those partition conditions.
declarations.Spec2Lean.instDecidableValidPartition: Register the partition decision procedure so Lean can check concrete partitions using decide.
declarations.Spec2Lean.member_starts_after: Every atom in a valid partition starts at or after the partition’s initial boundary.
declarations.Spec2Lean.partition_sound: Every position inside a valid partition belongs to exactly one of its atoms. This proves there are no character-range gaps or overlaps.
declarations.Spec2Lean.references_grounded: Every atom in a valid partition has at least one reference, and each reference is a known ID. Known IDs include explicit unresolved records.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.ids: The allowed claim and unresolved record IDs for this concrete source snapshot.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mtSHA256: The recorded SHA-256 identifier of the archived Semantics bytes. Python verifies the hash; Lean does not prove the hash computation.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mtAtoms: The generated source-character partition for Semantics. Unextracted intervals are explicitly unresolved.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mt_valid: Lean checks that this concrete Semantics partition is structurally valid.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mt_all_positions: Every Unicode scalar position in the Semantics snapshot belongs to exactly one recorded interval.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.mt_references: Every interval in the Semantics partition has nonempty, known references, including explicit unresolved references.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.conceptsSHA256: The recorded SHA-256 identifier of the archived Concepts bytes. Python verifies the hash; Lean does not prove the hash computation.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.conceptsAtoms: The generated source-character partition for Concepts. Unextracted intervals are explicitly unresolved.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.concepts_valid: Lean checks that this concrete Concepts partition is structurally valid.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.concepts_all_position: Every Unicode scalar position in the Concepts snapshot belongs to exactly one recorded interval.
declarations.Spec2Lean.Snapshot.concepts_references: Every interval in the Concepts partition has nonempty, known references, including explicit unresolved references.
